identity.mechanic: This unit's **host** is the biggest friendly unit in front of it (the left one on a tie). Only back-row units have anyone in front of them, so a climber in the front row has no host. The host is checked again whenever the board changes, fights included. A climber with no host just stands. At the very end of End of Turn, after every other effect, each climber gains half of its host's **biggest permanent gain this round**, permanently, and at least +1/+1 if the host gained anything. "Biggest" means most Attack plus Health in one gain. "This round" means since your last End of Turn, so lasting gains won in the last fight count. A gain from rising never makes another unit rise. A golden climber rises with its host's two biggest gains.

keywords.name: Host
keywords.text: in card text means any friendly unit that has at least one unit climbing it. Hosts can be of any tribe, or neutral.

identity.plays: The Ivy and Mistletoe don't win by themselves. They make whatever you're already building stronger. Your front row holds the real bodies, often another tribe's carry. Your three back slots hold climbers, which grow with whichever front unit is biggest in front of them, and each card does one more thing with that link. Honeysuckles feed their host and get half of it back. Mistletoe drains the host's Attack into the safe back row. Dodder hangs on the enemy instead. The decisions are where to put each unit, which three climbers get the back row, and which carry to hang them on. Each staggered back slot sits in front of two front slots, so B1, B2 and B3 each choose between two hosts. F2 and F3 can carry two climbers each, and you control which front unit is biggest.

units.name: Dodder Seedling
units.text: Start of Combat: take 1 Attack from the enemy across, for the fight.

units.name: Young Ivy
units.text: Climb. Start of Combat: give its host +2 Health for the fight. After its hosts have gained stats permanently 3 times in all, this becomes **Adult Ivy**, keeping its stats. The count is Young Ivy's own and never resets when its host changes.
units.golden: 2/4. +4 Health. Becomes a golden Adult Ivy.

units.name: Ivy Bush
units.text: Start of Turn: gain +1/+1 for each unit climbing this.

units.name: Woodbine
units.text: Climb. End of Turn: give its host +1/+1, or +3/+3 if Woodbine has never given to that unit before.

units.name: Hop Bine
units.text: Climb. Once a turn, when you buy a unit of its host's tribe, gain 1 gold.

units.name: Blackcap
units.text: When played: give a friendly unit Climb permanently.

units.name: Well-Connected Ivy
units.text: Climb. When played: if it has a host of a tribe, Discover a unit of that tribe (your tier or lower).

units.name: Kissing Bough
units.text: Climb. Berries 4. End of Turn: pick a berry to give its host +3/+3. With no berries left, this sells for 3 gold.

units.name: Apple Mistletoe
units.text: Climb. Start of Combat: take half its host's Attack for the fight, and give the host that much Health. Its attacks ignore Shield.
units.golden: 4/8. Gives the host twice that Health.

units.name: Ivy-clad Ruin
units.text: Your front-row units with Climb climb the biggest unit beside them.
units.golden: 4/16. Your climbers also rise with their host's two biggest gains.

units.name: Missel
units.text: Start of Combat: give Shield to your two biggest hosts. Enemies with Swoop must attack this while it lives.

units.name: Night-Scented Honeysuckle
units.text: Climb. End of Turn: give each of your hosts +2/+2.

units.name: Traveller's Joy
units.text: Climb. Whenever a host gains stats in a fight, each unit climbing it gains half as much, for the fight. These fight gains are not rising, and never pass on to other units.

units.name: The Honourable Viscum Highbough
units.text: Climb, but only while his host is your biggest unit, Viscum included. Instead of the usual rise, at the very end of End of Turn he gains every permanent gain his host made this round, in full.

units.name: Old Man's Beard
units.text: Climb. When its host dies, gain the host's Attack and Health for the fight.

units.name: Barley-Sugar Twiner
units.text: Climb. End of Turn: its host gains its biggest gain this round again.

units.name: Lady Hedera Overlook
units.text: Climb. End of Turn: if her host's tribe isn't in her guest-book, sign it in. Then give each of your hosts +2/+2 for each signature.

units.name: Cousin Dodder
units.text: Whenever this attacks, first take a quarter of the biggest enemy's Attack and Health; it keeps them permanently.

units.name: Ivy of the Grand Oak
units.text: Climb. Start of Combat: each of your hosts gains the Attack and Health of every unit climbing it, for the fight.

extras.name: Adult Ivy
extras.text: (Young Ivy's grown form): Climb; rises with its host's two biggest gains. Golden Adult Ivy: four biggest.

extras.name: Notes on the rules
extras.text: the guest-book stays with Lady Hedera through moves and triples. Neutral units have no tribe, so they never sign the guest-book, pay Hop Bine or guide Well-Connected Ivy. Cousin Dodder's enemy loses the stats only for that fight, because boards are recorded.

builds.name: A. The Patron (one carry)
builds.text: You pick one big unit from any tribe (an Ooze that has eaten, a Fairy on two Rings, a Hunter after a Take) and put it in F2 or F3, so that two back slots climb it. The pieces are Woodbine and Night-Scented Honeysuckle to feed it, Barley-Sugar Twiner to repeat its biggest gain, and the Honourable Viscum Highbough, who copies every gain in full. Viscum is snobbish enough to limit himself: if he ever becomes your biggest unit, he loses his host. To keep him rising, you keep the carry bigger than him. A typical board: Missel, the carry and two tanks in front; Viscum, Twiner and Woodbine behind.

builds.name: B. The Season (a mixed board)
builds.text: You spread climbers over hosts of three or four tribes. Hop Bine pays you for buying whatever its host is. Well-Connected Ivy Discovers from the host's tribe, which helps you find new tribes. Each turn you move Lady Hedera behind a host of a tribe she hasn't signed yet; at five signatures every host gains +10/+10 a turn. Woodbine takes the same shuffle well, giving +3/+3 to each patron it hasn't flattered before, while Ivy Bush rewards climbers that stay put. Blackcap grafts Climb onto other tribes' back-row units: a climbing Bird banks its echoes and then Flies South to double them.

builds.name: C. Parasites
builds.text: Dodder Seedling and Cousin Dodder take from the enemy. Apple Mistletoe moves the host's Attack into the back row and makes the host tankier, which pairs well with a Bog Mire or a Hunkering host. Mistletoe's attacks ignore Shield, the oath it never swore. Old Man's Beard inherits the host when it falls. Traveller's Joy makes fight gains rise too: the Health that Mistletoe gives the host comes half back to every climber on it. Cousin Dodder's takes are permanent, so a climber on Cousin Dodder rises with them. If Cousin Dodder is your biggest unit, Viscum gains every take in full at End of Turn.

builds.name: D. The Trellis (late, wide)
builds.text: From Tier 4, Ivy-clad Ruin lets front-row climbers climb beside them, so one board can hold five climbers on two hosts. The finish is Ivy of the Grand Oak: at Start of Combat each host takes in its climbers' combined stats, so the stats stored in the back row join the front line.

builds.name: In a lobby
builds.text: With Hedgerow folk, Pass X targets your rightmost unit, so a host in that seat echoes every Pass. Oozes give the biggest single gains, so build A loves them. Fairies' Ring stats are standing stats, not gains, so they don't rise; a Shy Fairy is a poor host. Birds' Swoop is the main threat to climbers, and Missel answers it. With Bog folk, a Mired, Bitter host plus Mistletoe means the front holds while the back hits. With Hunters, each Take landing next turn is one big gain to echo.

risks: **The echo multiplies other tribes' carries.** A golden Ooze that eats a 40/40 is a huge single gain. The lever is ready: half becomes a third, or "biggest gain" stays capped at one a round. Watch Viscum on an Ooze.

**The back row is a bottleneck.** 13 of 19 units climb and only three slots climb before Ivy-clad Ruin. Shops in the middle game will often offer climbers you can't place. That is the intended choice, but it may read as dead draws. If it does, move one climber (Hop Bine) to also work from the front row.
**Mono-tribe is weak by design.** The tribe's own hosts are Ivy Bush, Ivy-clad Ruin, Missel and the Dodders. Paired with a weak tribe in the lobby, it may have nothing worth climbing.
**Readability.** Host links shift as units die. The screen must draw the vine from climber to host and animate the rise at End of Turn, or nobody sees the tribe working.
**Contested pool.** One or two climbers help any board, so other players may take them as splashes and drain copies.
**Early-game tempo is thin.** Half of a +1/+1 rounds down, so early climbers mostly rise by the +1/+1 floor; the first turns still lean on Dodder Seedling and Ivy Bush.
**Viscum can feel bad** when he loses his host by growing. That is intended, but it needs clear feedback.
**Open:** whether "biggest unit in front" handles rows correctly in every edge case once back-row access rules are settled, and whether Ruin's sideways climbing should also reach the back row.

tier_check.note: Dodder Seedling has a body of 4 and swings about 2 in a fight (target 2.4). Young Ivy has a small body and gives its host 2 Health in a fight. Late on, Adult Ivy rises 4–10 a turn, above 0.4 body. **I broke this on purpose:** Young Ivy is the seed, all of its value is borrowed and it uses one of three back slots.

Ivy Bush gives +2/+2 a turn with two climbers, plus their echo. Woodbine gives 2 a turn, or 6 for each host it hasn't given to before. Hop Bine gives about 1 gold a turn, worth a third of a unit. All within 0.3–1 body.

Kissing Bough gives +6 a turn for four turns, then 3 gold (target about 5.6). Blackcap and Well-Connected Ivy are one-off pieces worth about one body. Apple Mistletoe nets about half its host's Attack in a fight: on target at a 10-Attack host, high late. **On purpose:** it scales with a host from another tribe, not with itself.

Night-Scented Honeysuckle gives 8–12 a turn (target 11). Missel's two Shields are worth about 16–20 in a fight (target 17). Ivy-clad Ruin has a body of 10, above 8.5 on purpose because it is a host and tank whose text adds capacity, not stats. I changed the shape: two enablers (Traveller's Joy, Missel) instead of a second buffer, because climbers need hosts that survive and fights that rise.
Viscum gives about 20–30 a turn (target 24, top 60 on a Dodder or Ooze carry). Old Man's Beard inherits about 40–60 in a fight (target 48). Barley-Sugar Twiner repeats about 24 a turn.

Lady Hedera gives 36–60 a turn plus echoes at three to five signatures (target 56). Cousin Dodder keeps 50–75 a fight permanently. Ivy of the Grand Oak moves about 100 into the front in a fight (target 84). Golden ceilings stay at about ×2. Runaway check: Cousin Dodder takes from the enemy, Viscum loses his host once he is the biggest, and rising never chains, so nothing feeds its own source.

rationale: **Gaps.** Every tribe's payoff feeds its own units, yet every lobby mixes five tribes, so no card makes another tribe's carry better and nothing rewards a mixed board.
**Gaps.** The back row is only a waiting room (only Swoop cares about it), and there is no shared buff multiplier.
**Filled with one keyword:** climbers live in the back row and rise with the front unit in front of them, of any tribe. That makes the tribe a bridge, a multiplier and the back row's purpose at once.

**The host is "the biggest unit in front of it"** rather than a chosen link. It uses Bramble's existing words and board, it is readable on a recorded board, and choosing whom to climb becomes arranging the board.

**Rising is half of the biggest gain this round, at End of Turn.** It doesn't depend on play order (no trap with Start of Turn gains), a stream of small buffs can't multiply, and it rewards Johnny for concentrating buffs.
**Rising never chains**, which removes loops and runaway with one sentence.
**Only three back slots is the scarcity on purpose**, and Ivy-clad Ruin at Tier 4 releases it as the tribe's first multiplier.

**Roles first, in three directions:** friend (feed the host), parasite (take from the host or the enemy), patron (one carry). Each direction got a Tier 1–3 entry, a Tier 4–5 engine and a Tier 6 finish.
**The economy is a bridge** (Hop Bine, Well-Connected Ivy) because this tribe's real need is finding its host's tribe.
**Missel answers Swoop**, the existing keyword that threatens climbers. Traveller's Joy brings fight gains in for the parasite build.
**Capstones reward a behaviour, not a number:** rotate patrons (Hedera), grow from the enemy (Dodder), empty the back row into the front (Grand Oak). Viscum limits himself by snobbery.
**Names and flavor came last**, fitted to the slots: the snob on the biggest host, the gatecrasher on the enemy, the poet flattering new patrons.

changes.what: Rise now gives at least +1/+1 when the host gained anything.
changes.why: Half of an early +1/+1 rounds to nothing, so climbers stood still in rounds 2 to 5.

changes.what: Says its 3-gain count is its own and never resets; gives its host +2 Health in fights.
changes.why: The counter's behaviour on a host change was unclear; the small fight effect lets it hold a slot early.

changes.what: The +3/+3 goes to a unit Woodbine has never given to, not a host different from last turn.
changes.why: Swapping between two back slots every turn earned the bonus for free, so swapping was always right.

changes.what: Drops the word 'rise'; says its fight gains are not rising and never pass on.
changes.why: It said climbers rise in fights, which clashed with the rule that rising never chains.

changes.what: Rises at End of Turn with every gain in full, replacing his half rise; host must be your biggest unit, him included.
changes.why: When he rose and whether full added to half were unclear; the old host rule let him outgrow his host.
